question: A 12-year-old girl (weight 40 kg) is brought to the emergency department after ingesting 30 tablets of paracetamol 500 mg (total 15,000 mg = 375 mg/kg) approximately 5 hours ago. She appears well and denies abdominal pain. Which of the following is the MOST appropriate next step?

answers.text: Reassure and discharge as she is clinically asymptomatic with no abdominal pain at 5 hours

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Clinical well-being in the first 24 hours is characteristic of paracetamol poisoning — it does NOT indicate safety. The toxic dose (>150 mg/kg) has been exceeded, and hepatocellular necrosis from NAPQI accumulation peaks at 72–96 hours after ingestion. Discharging this patient is dangerous.

answers.text: Send a serum paracetamol level now (at least 4 hours post-ingestion), plot on the Rumack-Matthew nomogram, and initiate N-acetylcysteine (NAC) if the level falls above the treatment line

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. The Rumack-Matthew nomogram is valid only for levels taken ≥4 hours after ingestion (levels before 4 hours do not reflect peak absorption). At 5 hours, a serum level is valid and should be plotted. Since the ingested dose exceeds the toxic threshold of 150 mg/kg, there is a high probability NAC will be required. Early NAC initiation before hepatotoxicity is highly protective.

answers.text: Measure a serum paracetamol level immediately and plot it on the nomogram at the 1-hour time point

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The Rumack-Matthew nomogram is not valid for levels taken before 4 hours post-ingestion, as absorption may be incomplete and levels do not yet reflect peak concentration. A level at the current time (5 hours) should be plotted at the correct time point on the nomogram.

answers.text: Administer activated charcoal 1 g/kg as she presents within 24 hours of ingestion

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Activated charcoal is most effective within 1–2 hours of ingestion. At 5 hours post-ingestion, absorption is largely complete and charcoal has minimal benefit. The priority at this stage is serum paracetamol level measurement and assessment against the Rumack-Matthew nomogram to decide on NAC.

overallFeedback.feedback: Key rules: Rumack-Matthew nomogram valid only ≥4 hours post-ingestion. Clinical well-being in early hours does NOT mean safety — hepatic injury peaks at 72–96 hours. NAC is the antidote and is most protective when started early.

Correct. The Rumack-Matthew nomogram is the decision tool: serum paracetamol level ≥4 hours post-ingestion plotted against the treatment line. Clinical appearance in the first 24 hours is deceptive — the toxic dose (>150 mg/kg) mandates urgent evaluation and likely NAC.
